name: Lucis

soc2_evidence.signal: No SOC 2 mention found; site advertises HDS certification, ISO 27001 and GDPR compliance instead (European compliance path)

hiring_signals: Platform Engineering (Paris, 6+ yrs) - listed on YC jobs page
Founders Associate, Customer Excellence, Head of Growth (no dedicated security/GRC roles)

contacts.name: Lucis (generic)
contacts.source: https://www.lucis.life/ (email surfaced in public web results referencing lucis.life contact)

pitch_note: Paris-based consumer health company already on the European compliance track (ISO 27001, HDS, GDPR) and freshly funded with a $20M Series A, so it exceeds the <$10M lean-startup profile; SOC 2 is a secondary need unless they pursue US B2B customers.

name: Pelica

soc2_evidence.signal: Site states Pelica is SOC 2 Type II certified, HIPAA-aligned with full BAA coverage; SOC 2 Type II report available on request
YC profile content also references 'HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II, and RADV-defensible'

pitch_note: Disqualified for Type I outreach: already advertises SOC 2 Type II plus HIPAA/BAA coverage on its homepage. Only angle would be ongoing audit/renewal services.

name: Code Four

soc2_evidence.signal: No SOC 2 badge or claim found; marketing centers on FBI CJIS compliance (AES-256, audit logging, RBAC). /security page returns 404.
Company published a Medium post arguing SOC 2 alone doesn't cover CJIS - implies they have not obtained SOC 2 and lean on CJIS positioning

aws_evidence: Terms of service state the platform is 'hosted exclusively in AWS GovCloud' with AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit (https://codefour.us/termofservice)
pitch_note: AWS GovCloud-native govtech with 25 police-department customers, a fresh $2.7M seed, founding-engineer hiring, and no SOC 2 - larger agencies and city procurement will ask for it alongside CJIS. Note: their own content downplays SOC 2 vs CJIS, so pitch it as complementary to their CJIS story.

name: Bayesline

soc2_evidence.signal: No SOC 2 mention found on site, YC profile, or in web results; sells cloud-deployed analytics to hedge funds and institutional asset managers who run vendor due-diligence/SOC report reviews
About page and launch describe cloud-deployed GPU analytics for institutional investors with no trust/compliance page found

hiring_signals: Full Stack Founding Engineer (NYC, $150K-$250K, 1-2% equity) - YC jobs page
Job/launch materials emphasize cloud deployment into client environments
aws_evidence: Cloud-deployed GPU analytics solution that 'deploys on client cloud' per YC profile; no explicit provider named (https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/bayesline)
pitch_note: No SOC 2 found, yet its buyers are hedge funds and institutional asset managers whose vendor due diligence explicitly requires SOC reports; $2M seed and a founding-engineer hire make this the classic pre-attestation moment. Cloud deployment into client environments raises the compliance stakes further.

name: Saturn

soc2_evidence.signal: Saturn's own security page metadata: 'Saturn puts security at it's heart with data residency, SOC 2 certification and a privacy focus'

pitch_note: Disqualified: already advertises SOC 2 certification on its security page and just closed a $15M Series A ($17.8M total), putting it past both the compliance and funding thresholds of the ICP.

name: Paasa

soc2_evidence.signal: No SOC 2 mention found; site emphasizes SEBI RIA registration, RBI LRS compliance and SIPC insurance via IBKR - consumer fintech regulatory framing, not SOC 2

pitch_note: Lean pre-seed fintech with a founding-engineer opening and no SOC 2, but it is an India-based consumer investing app whose compliance needs run through SEBI/RBI rather than US enterprise procurement - marginal ICP fit unless they court B2B wealth-manager partners.

name: Finosu

soc2_evidence.signal: No SOC 2 badge or claim found on site or in web results; sells B2B to regulated consumer lenders and pitches 'compliance default' loan servicing (state lending licenses, loan book audit prep) - a segment where lenders and bank partners demand SOC 2

Infra Engineer job says 'everything is compliant default' but lists no SOC 2 certification, and notes current priorities are cost reduction and observability 'over compliance certifications' - attestation gap is explicit

hiring_signals: Infra Engineer (NYC, $125K-$200K, 0.25%-2% equity) - AWS, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, Redis, Datadog-to-Grafana migration
aws_evidence: Infra Engineer job posting explicitly lists Amazon Web Services (AWS) as a required skill, plus Kubernetes scaling work (https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/finosu/jobs/TKx1Llu-infra-engineer)

contacts.name: Mark Ricciardi
contacts.source: https://www.finosu.com/ (publicly listed demo contact surfaced in web results)

pitch_note: Best lead in the slice: AWS-native (explicit in their Infra Engineer posting) consumer-loan servicer selling into regulated lenders, marketing 'compliance default' with zero SOC 2 attestation, pre-seed lean, and actively hiring the exact infra role that owns a Type I readiness project.

name: Moreta

soc2_evidence.signal: No SOC 2 or PCI certification claims found; FAQ/site only reference generic 'banking-grade infrastructure'

hiring_signals: No open positions listed (YC profile shows 0 jobs; is_hiring false)
pitch_note: Consumer travel-payments app with no B2B/enterprise buyers, no open roles, and no funding beyond the YC standard deal - PCI DSS is its more urgent framework than SOC 2, and hiring/growth signals are flat.
